entries.name: ArcReel
entries.use_for: Self-host a pipeline that turns novels or scripts into storyboards, video clips and editable drafts.
entries.why: Keeps characters consistent across shots, tracks cost, and exports drafts for further editing.
entries.summary: A self-hosted workbench that runs content analysis, asset creation, storyboards, media generation and export as a reviewable pipeline. It reuses reference images across shots, lets you redo single assets, and shows cost. Runs with Docker Compose.
entries.best_for: Building or forking a short-video or AI drama production tool with agent steps and several model providers.
entries.not_for: Capcut export: the README says the export targets the mainland China version of Jianying, and CapCut is untested. Docs are mainly Chinese. AGPL-3.0.

entries.name: auto-editor
entries.use_for: Automatically cut silence and dead air from videos and export to editors or rendered files.
entries.why: Popular, actively maintained CLI for automated rough cuts; exports to Premiere, Resolve and FCP.
entries.summary: Command-line tool that analyzes audio loudness (and other methods) to cut silence and dead space from video and audio, with a margin option to tune pacing. Exports edits to editors or renders files, and ships agent skills.
entries.best_for: Automating first-pass rough cuts for talking-head videos, podcasts and lectures.
entries.not_for: Only removes or speeds sections based on analysis; it is not a full editor or creative tool. Judgment on content still needs manual editing.

entries.name: Banana Slides
entries.use_for: Generate editable slide decks from an idea, outline or documents using image-generation models.
entries.why: Renders each page with an image model, accepts custom template images, and exports PPTX.
entries.summary: Banana Slides is an AI-native presentation generator. You give it an idea, outline, documents or template images, and it builds pages with image-generation models. You can edit by chatting, select regions to change, and export to PPTX or video. It runs locally with Docker. The README is mainly Chinese.
entries.best_for: Self-hosting or forking an AI slide generator with template control.
entries.not_for: Closed-source or SaaS use without care. It is AGPL-3.0, and it needs image and text model API access.

entries.name: Clypra
entries.use_for: Fork or study a Tauri video editor with a frame-accurate timeline and hardware-accelerated decoding.
entries.why: Rust decoding with GPU support and FFmpeg under a React 19 UI, MIT licensed.
entries.summary: A free desktop video editor built on Rust, Tauri v2 and React 19. It has a multi-track timeline, GPU decoding, waveforms, text overlays, filters, and exports to MP4, MOV, WebM and ProRes.
entries.best_for: A starting point or code reference for a native-feeling desktop video editor.
entries.not_for: An end-user app, not a library or SDK, so there is no embeddable editing API in the README. Performance claims are the project's own.

entries.name: Concat
entries.use_for: Edit video locally with captions, voices and cutouts, or script edits through a JSON-RPC API.
entries.why: A Rust engine with a GPU compositor and a JSON-RPC API that agents can drive.
entries.summary: A free video editor for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android. It has local Whisper captions, text-to-speech with voice cloning, background removal, keyframes, effects and multi-track editing. Export reaches 4K with H.264, HEVC or AV1.
entries.best_for: A CapCut replacement without watermarks or accounts, or scripted and agent-driven video cutting.
entries.not_for: AGPL-3.0 license, which limits closed-source use. It is an editor app, not an embeddable video library. AI models download once in Settings.

entries.name: CorridorKey
entries.use_for: Key green or blue screen footage, recovering true foreground colour and soft alpha at edges.
entries.why: Predicts straight foreground colour and linear alpha, keeping hair, motion blur and translucency.
entries.summary: CorridorKey is a neural network that separates a foreground subject from a green screen. For each pixel it predicts the true foreground colour and a clean linear alpha, rather than a binary mask. It handles green or blue screens, scales to 4K and reads and writes 16-bit and 32-bit linear EXR.
entries.best_for: VFX and compositing work in Nuke, Fusion or Resolve where edge quality matters.
entries.not_for: Commercial use without reading the licence, which is non-standard. Blue-screen support is currently Torch-only.

entries.name: Diffusion Studio
entries.use_for: Let a coding agent edit video, add captions and build motion graphics by driving a code-based timeline.
entries.why: Video is defined as SolidJS code, so the canvas and the code stay in sync and agents can edit both.
entries.summary: A desktop app whose document source is SolidJS modules rendered to a video canvas. It registers an MCP server with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others, plus command-line tools so agents can watch footage, edit and render.
entries.best_for: Letting an agent cut footage, make promos or explainers, or clip long videos from plain-language requests.
entries.not_for: Desktop app for Apple Silicon macOS and Windows x64 only. Needs an agent to drive it. MPL-2.0 licensed.

entries.name: FastVideo
entries.use_for: Speed up inference and post-training of open video diffusion models like Wan and Hunyuan.
entries.why: Unified, actively developed framework for accelerated video generation; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: Framework for post-training and real-time inference of video diffusion models. Supports full and LoRA fine-tuning, data preprocessing, DMD2 distillation, sparse attention, and FSDP2 scalable training.
entries.best_for: Researchers and teams fine-tuning or serving open video DiT models like Wan or Hunyuan faster on GPUs.
entries.not_for: Needs substantial GPU resources and ML expertise; not an end-user video editor or hosted generation service.

entries.name: FFmpeg
entries.use_for: Decode, encode, transcode, mux and filter almost any audio/video format from the CLI or libav* libraries.
entries.why: The de facto media processing engine underneath most video tools; LGPL-2.1+ by default (verified LICENSE.md).
entries.summary: Collection of libraries (libavcodec, libavformat, libavutil, libavfilter and others) and command-line tools to decode, encode, transcode, mux, stream and filter audio, video and subtitles.
entries.best_for: Any server, app or script needing format conversion, transcoding, trimming, thumbnailing or streaming prep.
entries.not_for: CLI flags are complex and it is C code, so embedding requires care. Licensing depends on build options (LGPL or GPL), and it is not a GUI or editor.

entries.name: FFmpeg-Builds
entries.use_for: Download up-to-date static/shared FFmpeg builds for Windows and Linux in CI or apps
entries.why: Widely used source of nightly and release FFmpeg binaries (GPL/LGPL variants) built reproducibly via GitHub Actions.
entries.summary: Automatically built static and shared FFmpeg binaries for Windows and Linux x86_64 (master and latest release), produced via GitHub Actions in GPL and LGPL variants.
entries.best_for: Getting up-to-date FFmpeg binaries for CI, Docker images or bundled apps on Windows and Linux.
entries.not_for: Builds only for x86_64 Windows and Linux (no macOS); it distributes binaries, not an API. Check GPL versus LGPL variants for licensing.

entries.name: ffmpeg.wasm
entries.use_for: Run FFmpeg in the browser or Node via WebAssembly for client-side video conversion.
entries.why: Most widely used WASM port of FFmpeg; avoids a server for trimming, converting and thumbnailing.
entries.summary: Pure WebAssembly and JavaScript port of FFmpeg that records, converts and streams audio and video directly in browsers or Node.
entries.best_for: Client-side video or audio conversion, trimming and thumbnailing without sending files to a server.
entries.not_for: Slower than native FFmpeg and memory-limited in browsers; large files and heavy transcodes are impractical. README is brief and docs are external.

entries.name: FireRed-OpenStoryline
entries.use_for: Edit videos by chatting with an LLM agent that plans the cut, finds media, writes narration and picks music.
entries.why: Human-in-the-loop editing with reusable style skills and conversational refinement of clips, color and fonts.
entries.summary: An AI video editing agent that turns a natural-language request into a finished video. It searches for media, segments clips, writes a script, recommends music, voiceover and fonts, and lets you refine by conversation. You configure API keys in config.toml.
entries.best_for: Building or running a chat-driven video editor, especially for short narrated or commentary videos.
entries.not_for: Offline use or exact frame-level editing: it needs LLM and service API keys, and results depend on those models.

entries.name: go2rtc
entries.use_for: Restream and convert camera streams between RTSP, WebRTC, HLS, MSE and more.
entries.why: Zero-dependency streaming server widely used with Frigate/Home Assistant for low-latency camera video.
entries.summary: Zero-dependency camera streaming app that ingests many formats and protocols, outputs to popular formats, and restreams with low latency. Transcodes via FFmpeg only when needed, with two-way audio support.
entries.best_for: Restreaming IP cameras (RTSP to WebRTC, HLS, MSE), including Home Assistant and Frigate setups.
entries.not_for: Focused on camera-style streams; not a full media server with recording library or a general video platform. Some features depend on external FFmpeg.

entries.name: GStreamer
entries.use_for: Pipeline-based multimedia framework for building capture, transcoding, streaming and playback apps
entries.why: The standard plugin-based media pipeline framework on Linux and embedded devices; bindings for Rust, Python and more

license_verified.note: LICENSE is LGPL 2.1; some optional plugins with GPL deps are opt-in

entries.summary: GStreamer is a framework for streaming media; this repo holds all official community modules. It builds with Meson, which pulls mandatory dependencies (glib, zlib, libffi, libintl) and optional ones like ffmpeg, x264 and openh264 as subprojects. Docs, tutorials and API reference are on gstreamer.freedesktop.org.
entries.best_for: Building native media pipelines for playback, capture, transcoding or streaming in desktop, embedded or server apps.
entries.not_for: Simple one-off video conversion where the ffmpeg CLI is enough, or browser-only apps. Some plugins need system-provided optional dependencies to build.

entries.name: GSYVideoPlayer
entries.use_for: Add a full-featured video player to an Android app
entries.why: Wraps IJKPlayer, ExoPlayer and MediaPlayer behind one API with caching, danmaku, filters and fullscreen handling.
entries.summary: Android video player library that unifies IJKPlayer, ExoPlayer, MediaPlayer and optionally AliPlayer behind one API, with caching, danmaku, filters, fullscreen handling and optional DLNA casting.
entries.best_for: Android apps that need a feature-rich video player with list playback, caching and multiple engine options.
entries.not_for: Android only. The README is partly Chinese-oriented, and wrapping several engines adds size compared with using Media3/ExoPlayer directly.

entries.name: hls.js
entries.use_for: Play HLS (m3u8) streams in browsers that lack native HLS via Media Source Extensions.
entries.why: The standard HLS playback library on the web, used by most JS video players.
entries.summary: JavaScript library that plays HLS streams via Media Source Extensions in browsers without native HLS. Supports VOD, live with DVR, low-latency HLS, fMP4 and MPEG-TS, and codecs such as HEVC and AV1 subject to runtime support.
entries.best_for: Adding HLS (m3u8) playback to a web video element or custom player.
entries.not_for: Playback engine only with no UI or DRM tooling (use Shaka or Video.js for more). HLS only, not DASH.

entries.name: html-video
entries.use_for: Have a coding agent turn a prompt, article link or repo into a rendered MP4 from HTML.
entries.why: A meta-layer over render engines with one adapter interface, 21 templates and no per-render fees.
entries.summary: Works with your local coding agent to turn a prompt, article or GitHub repo into a storyboard and HTML frames, then renders a real MP4 on your machine. Hyperframes is the shipped engine using headless Chromium and ffmpeg; Remotion and others are planned. Includes templates and optional AI soundtrack.
entries.best_for: Generating explainer, promo or repo videos locally from an agent without paid render services.
entries.not_for: Only one render engine is shipped today. Others are listed as planned.

entries.name: HyperFrames
entries.use_for: Author videos as HTML/CSS/JS compositions and render them deterministically to MP4.
entries.why: Apache-2.0 HTML-to-video renderer designed for coding agents; a permissive alternative to Remotion-style workflows.
entries.summary: Open-source framework that turns HTML, CSS, media and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Used through a CLI, agent skills, or as a rendering core; targets uses like product videos, captions, chart animations and docs-to-video.
entries.best_for: Programmatic or AI-agent-authored videos where you can describe scenes in web tech and need repeatable renders.
entries.not_for: Renders compositions you author; it does not generate footage or act as a timeline editor. Requires a headless browser rendering pipeline and web-skill authoring.

entries.name: Hypit
entries.use_for: Let an agent turn a reference video into an editable, re-runnable workflow and render many variants.
entries.why: Clones the whole workflow with footage, captions and B-roll, not just a script breakdown.
entries.summary: Hypit gives agents like Claude Code and Codex a system to create video. Drop in a video and the agent rebuilds it as a composition with captions and effects tied to words. You can swap the host, hook or language and render many variants.
entries.best_for: Marketers and creators who want many variants of one ad or short-form video format.
entries.not_for: Anyone who needs clear license terms: the license is not a standard one. Model services you plug in are billed separately.

entries.name: LingBot-World
entries.use_for: Run an open world simulator that generates interactive video from camera or action input.
entries.why: Open weights for a video-based world model with minute-level memory and real-time use.
entries.summary: An open-source world simulator built from video generation, on top of Wan2.2. It targets diverse environments, minute-long consistency and interactive latency under one second at 16 fps. Base, Act and Fast variants are released.
entries.best_for: Researchers and builders experimenting with open interactive world models.
entries.not_for: No longer actively maintained. The README points to a newer repo, lingbot-world-v2, for updates.

entries.name: LivePortrait
entries.use_for: Animate a still portrait from a driving video or expressions
entries.why: Efficient Kuaishou/Kling portrait animation model with stitching and retargeting control; MIT-licensed code.
entries.summary: Official PyTorch implementation of a portrait animation model that drives a still image with a video or expressions, with stitching and retargeting control.
entries.best_for: Animating portraits and avatars from a reference face or driving video in research or creative pipelines.
entries.not_for: Requires GPU and model downloads, and face-animation misuse (deepfakes) raises ethical and legal concerns. Check model weight licensing before commercial use.

entries.name: LongCat-Video
entries.use_for: Generate text-to-video, image-to-video and long continued videos with one open 13.6B model.
entries.why: Natively trained on video continuation for minutes-long clips without quality drift.
entries.summary: A 13.6B-parameter video generation model that unifies text-to-video, image-to-video and video continuation. It uses a coarse-to-fine strategy and block sparse attention to produce 720p, 30fps video in minutes, and was tuned with multi-reward GRPO.
entries.best_for: Researchers and builders needing open, long-form video generation under an MIT license.
entries.not_for: Small GPUs or production use without evaluation. The model card says it was not evaluated for every downstream use.

entries.name: LTX-2
entries.use_for: Run and fine-tune an open audio-video generation model with synchronized sound.
entries.why: One DiT model produces video and audio together, with a LoRA trainer included.
entries.summary: Official Python inference and LoRA trainer package for LTX-2, a DiT-based audio-video foundation model. Setup uses uv and downloads roughly 66 GiB of weights from Hugging Face after accepting model terms. Linux with CUDA gives the fastest VAE backend.
entries.best_for: Teams with a strong GPU who want local, tunable text or image to video with audio.
entries.not_for: Small machines or tight storage. The license is custom (NOASSERTION) and weights are gated on Hugging Face.

entries.name: Mediabunny
entries.use_for: Read, write and convert MP4/WebM/MP3 and more in the browser with WebCodecs, no FFmpeg needed
entries.why: Pure-TypeScript media toolkit (successor to mp4-muxer/webm-muxer) for fast in-browser transcoding, trimming and muxing
entries.summary: Zero-dependency pure TypeScript toolkit for reading, writing and converting media (MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, MP3, HLS and more) in the browser using WebCodecs. Highly tree-shakable.
entries.best_for: Client-side video trimming, conversion and muxing in web apps without bundling FFmpeg.
entries.not_for: Relies on browser WebCodecs support, so formats and codecs follow what the runtime allows; not as format-complete as FFmpeg. Check its license terms.

entries.name: MediaMTX
entries.use_for: Ready-to-use media server and proxy to read, publish and route live video over RTSP, RTMP, WebRTC, HLS and SRT
entries.why: Single binary that converts between all common live-streaming protocols; the default self-hosted relay for cameras and live video
entries.summary: Zero-dependency live media server and proxy that publishes, reads, proxies, records and plays back streams across protocols such as SRT, WebRTC, RTSP, RTMP, HLS and MPEG-TS.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted relay for cameras and live video, converting between streaming protocols in a single binary.
entries.not_for: Not a transcoding pipeline or CDN and has no built-in app or UI. Large-scale distribution needs extra infrastructure.

entries.name: Motion Canvas
entries.use_for: Create animated explainer videos programmatically with TypeScript and a live-preview editor
entries.why: MIT-licensed code-to-video tool with a timeline editor; a fully open alternative for programmatic motion graphics
entries.summary: TypeScript library that programs vector animations with generator functions, paired with a real-time preview editor for syncing animations to voice-overs.
entries.best_for: Explainer and educational vector animation videos authored in code.
entries.not_for: Aimed at 2D informative animations, not general video editing or live-action footage. Requires TypeScript coding and a browser-based editor workflow.

entries.name: MoviePy
entries.use_for: Script video edits in Python: cut, concatenate, add titles, overlays and effects.
entries.why: Long-standing, simple Python API for programmatic editing; MIT licensed and actively maintained.
entries.summary: Python library for video editing: cuts, concatenation, titles, compositing and custom effects, reading and writing common formats including GIF. v2.0 introduced breaking changes, and v1 is unmaintained.
entries.best_for: Scripted video edits and batch processing in Python.
entries.not_for: Not real-time and can be slow on long videos; v1 code needs migration to v2. Heavy editing or precise frame work may be better with FFmpeg or PyAV directly.

entries.name: mpv
entries.use_for: Embed a capable video player in your app via libmpv, or script playback from the CLI
entries.why: libmpv powers many desktop players; plays nearly any format with GPU rendering and a Lua/JS scripting API.

license_verified.note: Copyright file: GPLv2+ by default, LGPLv2.1+ when built with -Dgpl=false

entries.summary: Free command-line media player supporting many formats, codecs and subtitles. Can be embedded via libmpv and scripted with Lua or JavaScript.
entries.best_for: Embedding a capable player in native apps or scripting playback from the CLI.
entries.not_for: Minimal built-in GUI and not for web embedding; GPL/LGPL licensing depends on build. Not an editor or streaming server.

entries.name: OpenMontage
entries.use_for: Let your coding assistant research, script, generate assets, edit and render finished videos.
entries.why: 12 pipelines and 100+ tools, and it can work with zero paid API keys using free stock and open footage.
entries.summary: OpenMontage turns an AI coding assistant into a video studio. The agent handles research, scripting, asset generation, editing and composition using Remotion, HyperFrames and FFmpeg. Free options include Piper TTS and open footage archives.
entries.best_for: You want an agent to produce explainer, promo or stock-footage videos end to end.
entries.not_for: AGPL-3.0. Higher-quality generated clips need paid model APIs. It is a pipeline for agents, not a video editor UI.

entries.name: OpenReel Video
entries.use_for: Run or fork a browser-based video editor with timeline, captions and export, no watermark.
entries.why: Editing and rendering happen on-device, with an optional AI editor using your own model keys.
entries.summary: OpenReel is an MIT-licensed video editor for the browser and desktop. It has a multi-track timeline, keyframes, transitions, captions with SRT import, audio mixing and export presets. An AI assistant can make reversible edits through your own endpoint.
entries.best_for: Self-hosting or forking a CapCut-style editor that keeps footage local.
entries.not_for: Library use inside another app. It is a full editor, and the desktop builds are alpha.

entries.name: OpenScreen
entries.use_for: Record the screen and turn it into polished product demos with auto zoom and captions.
entries.why: Free and MIT, with auto-zoom, on-device captions, and an MCP server and demo skill for agents.
entries.summary: A desktop app for recording the screen or a window, then editing with zooms, cursor effects, webcam overlay, annotations and speed control. It has offline captions and an optional AI editor using your own key.
entries.best_for: Making demo videos or PR walkthroughs, including from a coding agent through its skill and MCP server.
entries.not_for: Under active development, with possible breaking changes to the project format and CLI. An end-user app, not an embeddable library.

entries.name: OpenTimelineIO
entries.use_for: Read, write and convert editorial timelines between NLEs (EDL, FCP XML and more via adapters).
entries.why: ASWF industry-standard API and format for editorial timeline interchange.
entries.summary: OpenTimelineIO is an Academy Software Foundation framework and API for editorial timeline data, widely deployed in film and television. It is natively supported in most non-linear editing applications and integrated in game engines and content creation tools. It ships a Python package built on a C++ core.
entries.best_for: Exchanging or programmatically processing editorial timelines (cuts, clips, tracks) between NLEs and pipeline tools in VFX and post-production.
entries.not_for: Rendering or encoding video; it handles timeline structure, not media. The license grants no rights to Pixar or contributor trademarks.

entries.name: PersonaLive
entries.use_for: Animate a portrait image in real time from a driving video, for live streaming research.
entries.why: A CVPR 2026 diffusion framework that is real-time, streamable and can run for infinite length.
entries.summary: PersonaLive is a diffusion framework for expressive portrait image animation in live streaming. It generates streamable, infinite-length animations. The repo provides weight download scripts, ONNX weights, a WebUI with reference image replacement, and training code. A follow-up, EditaLive, adds full-body animation and editing.
entries.best_for: You research or prototype real-time talking-head or portrait animation and can run GPU models.
entries.not_for: The README says it is released for academic research only and warns against harmful use. Needs a conda setup and downloaded weights. Not a hosted product.

entries.name: Pixelle-Video
entries.use_for: Generate a full short video from just a topic: script, images, voice-over, music and final render.
entries.why: Swap models freely: ComfyUI or RunningHub workflows or direct APIs for image, video, TTS and vision.
entries.summary: Pixelle-Video turns a topic into a short video with the flow: script, image planning, per-frame processing, composition. It supports many LLMs, TTS engines and templates, portrait or landscape, and has digital-human and image-to-video pipelines. A Windows bundle runs without setup. README is mostly Chinese.
entries.best_for: Producing faceless explainer or short-form videos at scale, or building on a modular video pipeline.
entries.not_for: Needs API keys or ComfyUI services for generation. Quality depends on the models you pick. Docs lean Chinese.

entries.name: PyAV
entries.use_for: Pythonic bindings to FFmpeg libraries for frame-level decoding, encoding and muxing
entries.why: Direct access to FFmpeg packets and frames from Python without shelling out; used by torchvision, auto-editor and many ML pipelines
entries.summary: Pythonic binding for FFmpeg libraries giving direct access to containers, streams, packets, codecs and frames, with helpers to move data to NumPy and Pillow.
entries.best_for: Frame-level decoding, encoding and muxing in Python without shelling out to ffmpeg, such as ML data pipelines.
entries.not_for: Lower-level than MoviePy and requires understanding of codecs and FFmpeg concepts. Not for simple one-off conversions where the ffmpeg CLI suffices.

entries.name: Recordly
entries.use_for: Record the screen and edit it into a polished demo video with auto zoom, cursor effects and styled frames.
entries.why: Free recorder and editor for Mac, Windows and Linux with native capture helpers.
entries.summary: Recordly is a desktop app built on Electron that records and edits screen captures. It adds zoom suggestions, smooth cursor movement, webcam bubbles and styled backgrounds. Scenes render with PixiJS and export to MP4 or GIF. Project files keep the editor state.
entries.best_for: Product demos and walkthroughs, or as a codebase to fork for a screen-recording tool.
entries.not_for: Mainly an end-user app. Its license is listed as unclear (NOASSERTION), so check before reusing code. Linux cannot hide the cursor.

entries.name: ReelMimic
entries.use_for: Make a new video in the style of a reference video, using a crew of Claude Code or Codex agents.
entries.why: Breaks the reference into rhythm and shots, then parallel agents build and a fresh agent reviews each shot.
entries.summary: A local web app that analyzes a reference video (file, recording or YouTube link) for shot count, timing, transitions, colors and camera moves. It shows a plan, then up to six agents build the video in parallel and independent reviewers check each shot. Styles are single Markdown files.
entries.best_for: Creators who want a new video in the style of one they like, and already have Claude Code or Codex.
entries.not_for: Copying the original footage or characters, which it does not carry over. It needs Node 22.18+, Python, FFmpeg and your own agent subscription.

entries.name: Seedance 2.0 Skill OS
entries.use_for: Have a coding agent plan shots and write Seedance video prompts, then continue from an accepted clip.
entries.why: Routes a request to the right workflow: interview, prompt, sequence, continuation, references or retake.
entries.summary: An agent skill pack that turns an idea into a directed Seedance 2.0 video prompt. It covers shot planning, reference binding, first and last frame control and continuing from accepted footage. Your video provider does the generation.
entries.best_for: Anyone prompting Seedance 2.0 who wants repeatable prompts and continuity across clips.
entries.not_for: It generates prompts, not video. The README says live model scores and rendered-pilot results are still pending.

entries.name: Shaka Player
entries.use_for: Adaptive DASH and HLS playback in the browser with DRM, offline storage and captions
entries.why: Google-backed player library for adaptive streaming with Widevine/PlayReady DRM; the go-to when hls.js alone isn't enough
entries.summary: JavaScript library for adaptive DASH and HLS playback in browsers via MSE and EME, with offline storage in IndexedDB, DRM support and a goal of staying light and simple.
entries.best_for: Web video with adaptive streaming, DRM (Widevine, PlayReady) or offline playback.
entries.not_for: Playback library rather than a full player skin and heavier than hls.js for simple HLS. DRM requires license servers and browser support.

entries.name: TurboDiffusion
entries.use_for: Speed up video diffusion models like Wan 2.1 and 2.2 by 100 to 200 times on one GPU.
entries.why: Combines SageAttention, sparse-linear attention and timestep distillation, with released checkpoints and training code.
entries.summary: TurboDiffusion is the official implementation of a video generation acceleration framework. It uses SageAttention, Sparse-Linear Attention and rCM timestep distillation to cut end-to-end generation from minutes to seconds on a single RTX 5090. It provides TurboWan checkpoints at 480p and 720p.
entries.best_for: You run Wan-based video generation and need much faster inference.
entries.not_for: Models were trained on long English prompts, so other prompts need augmenting. Checkpoints and paper are not final. Needs a strong GPU.

entries.name: video-use
entries.use_for: Let a coding agent edit videos (cuts, captions, overlays) from natural language
entries.why: From the browser-use team: gives Claude Code/Codex a toolkit to transcribe, cut and render edits programmatically.
entries.summary: Toolkit that lets a coding agent such as Claude Code edit videos from natural language: cuts filler words and dead space, color grades, adds audio fades and burns subtitles, producing a final.mp4.
entries.best_for: Letting an AI coding agent do talking-head or montage editing from a folder of raw footage.
entries.not_for: Agent-driven pipeline, not a GUI editor; quality depends on the agent and transcription. A cloud-hosted version is only a waitlist per the README.

entries.name: Video.js
entries.use_for: Embed a customizable, skinnable HTML5 video player with HLS/DASH support and plugins.
entries.why: Mature open-source web player with a large plugin ecosystem; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: Modular, composable media player framework for web and React (v10 is stable). Supports HLS/DASH and plugins; the repo also offers an AI skill for version-matched docs.
entries.best_for: Web video players needing a customizable, skinnable UI and plugin ecosystem.
entries.not_for: v10 is a new modular design, so v7/v8 plugins and code may not carry over. Heavier than a bare engine like hls.js if you only need playback.

entries.name: Vidstack Player
entries.use_for: Accessible, customisable audio/video player components for React and web components
entries.why: Modern successor to Plyr/Vime: headless-friendly player UI with HLS, YouTube and Vimeo providers built in
entries.summary: Accessible, customizable audio/video player components for React and web components with HLS, YouTube and Vimeo providers. README states it is in security-only maintenance with patches until January 2028.
entries.best_for: Keeping existing Vidstack players secure while migrating to Video.js 10.
entries.not_for: New projects should not start here: only security patches are merged and teams moved to Video.js 10.

entries.name: Wan 2.2
entries.use_for: Generate videos from text or images with open-weight diffusion models you can self-host.
entries.why: Leading open-weight video generation model family under Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: Open-weight video generation models from Wan, using a Mixture-of-Experts diffusion design; supports text-to-video and image-to-video with code and weights hosted on GitHub, Hugging Face and ModelScope.
entries.best_for: Self-hosting open text- or image-to-video generation with local GPUs.
entries.not_for: Requires large GPU memory and setup; results and speed trail hosted services for casual users. Review model license terms for your use.

entries.name: yt-dlp
entries.use_for: Download video and audio from YouTube and thousands of other sites from the CLI or Python.
entries.why: The maintained youtube-dl successor with the broadest site coverage; embeddable as a Python module.
entries.summary: Feature-rich command-line audio and video downloader supporting thousands of sites, forked from youtube-dl. Offers format selection, subtitles, post-processing, SponsorBlock, output templates and a Python API.
entries.best_for: Downloading or archiving media from supported sites in scripts or apps.
entries.not_for: Site extractors break when sites change, requiring frequent updates. Downloading may violate site terms or copyright; it is a downloader, not a player.
